newsitem.title: USA: U.S. April real earnings fell 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. April real earnings fell 0.9 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, fell 0.9 percent in April, the Labor Department said Thursday.
The April decrease followed a revised 0.4 percent rise in March real average weekly earnings. Previously, the department reported that March real earnings rose 0.1 percent.
The April fall stems from a 0.9 percent drop in average weekly hours and a 0.1 percent decline in average hourly earnings, the Labor Department said.

Real earnings last fell in January, when they dropped 1.8 percent. Average weekly hours also had not declined since January, when they fell 1.7 percent, and average hourly earnings had not fallen since October, when they were also down 0.1 percent.
Real average weekly earnings in April were 2.2 percent above the April 1996 level and the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers was unchanged last month, Labor reported.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $259.28 in April, versus a revised $261.75 in March and $253.95 in April 1996.
The department had previously reported March weekly earnings at $261.

In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $420.04 in April, compared with a revised $424.04 in March and $402 in April last year. The deparment had previously reported March current dollar earnings at $422.82.
